_note: Illustrative what-ifs, not measured outcomes or predictions. Alerts/dispatch are simulated. No lives-saved claims. Full arithmetic and sources: submission/IMPACT.md (all URLs fetched 14 Nov 2026).

flood.headline: 12 hours earlier = an alert before the first death. Published warning curves put ~EUR 1.1 bn of Valencia's EUR 4.8 bn insured loss within reach (illustrative: 22% x EUR 4.8 bn).

scenarios.people: before at least 146 of the 156 pre-20:11 deaths
before the rain peak; relies on forecasts (EFAS/AEMET), not my observed signal

flood.lives_context: Ahr 2021 peer-reviewed simulation: modelled deaths up to 80% lower with timely warning + evacuation, 24.3% with better warning spread alone (Rocha Silva et al. 2025, NHESS). Not applied to Valencia.
flood.days_claim: Rain signal arrives ~2 days before the first post-storm radar map (31 Oct) and ~4 days before the Copernicus EMS province-wide extent map (2 Nov); 99% cloud blinded optical. Sentinel-1 was on a 12-day repeat with one satellite.

fire.case: Alberta: Horse River (Fort McMurray) May 2016 + 2023 season
fire.headline: The data flags May months ahead: staffing by 15 April instead of 1 May gives 16 more days of readiness. Every escape prevented spares ~65,000 ha (illustrative, Alberta 2023), and one escaped May fire cost $8.9 bn in 2016.

baseline.escape_rule: 3% of fires cause 97% of area (Stocks et al. 2002)

fire.caveat: MNP (2017): initial attack on Horse River was immediate; can't say an alternative would have changed the outcome. Escapes prevented is an assumption.

field.case: 2012 US drought, Iowa; Story County steepest 92 squares
field.headline: In a 2012-type drought, rye on Story County's 92 steepest squares is worth ~$1.2 M net (illustrative: +11.1 bu/acre x $6.89 - $32/acre), and my map is ready before planting, not 11 months after.
field.lead_time: Per-pixel next-season map ~Feb (once prior CDL is out), before planting; CDL for the season arrives ~11 months later; Prospective Plantings is state-level (31 Mar).
